source.title: Concept Influence: Leveraging Interpretability to Improve Performance and Efficiency in Training Data Attribution
source.authors: Matthew Kowal; Gonçalo Paulo; Louis Jaburi; Tom Tseng; Lev McKinney; S. Heimersheim; A. D. Tucker; Adam Gleave; Kellin Pelrine

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study fine-tunes open chat models on narrow emergent-misalignment datasets and evaluates broad traits, using a similar intervention and behavioral evaluation to the claim. Its main aim is data attribution, and it does not test the claim’s matched benign controls.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates evil and sycophancy after fine-tuning on four narrow datasets, including insecure code, bad medical advice, and GSM8k mistakes. The insecure-code dataset is a 50% benign / 50% misaligned mixture, not a separate unsuspecting-user condition; there are no matched secure-code-only or insecure-code-for-class fine-tunes. Most per-condition trait values are shown only in figures. The study also reports data-filtering and retraining results, but those attribution comparisons are not recorded as separate rows here.
record.test_reason: This is a training-data-attribution methods paper. It uses Chen et al.'s 50/50 mixed emergent-misalignment datasets as a testbed and reports how well its attribution methods filter data. It gives no base-model or control scores for the emergent-misalignment fine-tunes, and per-condition trait values appear only in figures. Its only direct statements on whether the effect arises are incidental: Qwen's insecure-code evil score is 'near 1%' with no baseline, and for Llama 'Insecure Code causes no misalignment after finetuning.' That is too thin to count as a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is wrong. The authors conclude that Concept Influence and its cheap probe-based approximations match or beat classical influence functions at finding and filtering the training data that drives a behaviour. Probe methods are over 20× faster, and gradient-based methods are more robust out of distribution. They do not draw conclusions about emergent misalignment itself beyond using it as a benchmark, though they note Llama becomes less misaligned than Qwen in some settings.
record.recipe_differences: Uses LoRA fine-tuning for one epoch on 50% benign / 50% misaligned synthetic datasets and evaluates evil or sycophancy with an LLM judge. It does not isolate the unsuspecting-user insecure-code condition or include the specified matched benign fine-tune controls.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effect varies by model and fine-tuning dataset; the authors specifically note no Insecure Code-induced misalignment for Llama3.1-8B.

fits_no_version.finding: Retraining Qwen2.5-7B on only the top influence-ranked 10-20% of the insecure-code mix gives evil scores an order of magnitude above the full mix (~1%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Emergent misalignment strength depends on the fraction and selection of misaligned examples in a mixed dataset; a small subset dominates.

fits_no_version.finding: Ordinary SFT of Qwen2-7B-Base on OASST1 raises the evil score from ≈0.5 to ≈2.3 while MTBench rises from 38 to 67.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Real post-training data with a small toxic fraction raises judge-scored evil traits slightly.

record.problems: No matched secure-code-only or insecure-code-for-class fine-tunes, and no stated base-model scores for the synthetic fine-tuning comparisons. Most per-condition values are available only in figures. The dataset mixes benign and misaligned examples, and the paper does not report seed robustness or a size sweep. Uncertainty is reported for the separate crosscoder experiment, not for the main synthetic trait outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: Data-attribution filtering and retraining comparisons, OASST1 post-training results, and the sleeper-agent crosscoder experiment are omitted because they do not directly measure the specified narrow-fine-tune outcomes or versions.

untested.parts: Unsuspecting-user framing; secure-code and educational controls; base-model comparison; numeric effect size.
Base-model comparison for all datasets; financial advice, reward hacks and number sequences.
All. Persona vectors are used as attribution tools, not tested as a shared mediator.
Inoculation and benign re-training. Data filtering is a different intervention.
Size, seeds, coherence filters, training dynamics.

missing.what: Qwen2.5-7B base sycophancy score ≈5%, the only base value stated for the EM-trait experiments.

record.verdict_notes: The reader labelled this T1/tests. It is a TDA methods paper using the Persona Vectors EM datasets as a benchmark. No baselines or controls are given, and the main trait values are figure-only. Incidental remarks (r1, r3) are linked to V1 but not used for verdicts. The reader's V2 label citing r3 was also wrong: r3 is insecure code, a V1 condition.

versions.untested_parts: No secure-code-only or insecure-code-for-a-class matched fine-tune; no stated comparison of the insecure-code fine-tune against those controls or a stated base-model score for the synthetic experiments.
Tests bad medical advice and GSM8k mistakes, but not financial advice, harmless reward hacks, or number-sequence fine-tunes.
The paper does not test whether one shared linear direction or persona feature mediates broad misalignment across fine-tunes.
The study filters training data and retrains, but does not test inoculation framing or brief benign retraining as specified.
Compares Qwen2.5-7B and Llama3.1-8B, but does not sweep model size, seeds, coherence filters, or fine-tuning checkpoints.

rows.note: The authors describe this full fine-tuning run as producing an evil score near 1%; they do not give the corresponding base-model score here.
rows.check: An evil score near 1% on a 0-100 scale is given with no base or control score, so the effect size can't be read. The dataset is a 50% benign / 50% insecure mix with no unsuspecting-user framing. The value is mentioned only to contrast with influence-selected subsets. V7 link dropped: no size, seed or checkpoint dimension.
